strengths: Conceptual Elegance and Unification: The paper provides a clean, unified probabilistic perspective based on path-space Radon–Nikodym derivatives. It successfully unifies several seemingly distinct recent methods, including Itô density estimators, Feynman–Kac density estimators, twisted diffusion samplers (TDS), and Feynman–Kac correctors (FKC).

Sound Theoretical Analysis: The paper clearly articulates why naive discretizations of path density ratios suffer from severe variance misalignment when diffusion coefficients vary across time, and introduces an analytical reference process to resolve this issue. Proposition A.2 rigorously bounds the discretization error at O(sqrt(Delta t)).

Broad Applicability: RNE naturally accommodates tasks including density estimation, inference-time annealing, product-of-experts composition, and reward-tilting with non-differentiable objectives (e.g., QED and SA scores in drug design), as well as extending conceptually to discrete diffusion / CTMCs.

Comprehensive Experiments: The method is validated across diverse domains, including analytical GMM density estimation, molecular conformation annealing (Alanine Dipeptide, Lennard-Jones), and multi-target structure-based drug design (SBDD).
weaknesses: Incremental Practical Margin over FKC: While RNE generalizes FKC and affords extra flexibility via the proposal/target drift parameters (ca, cb), the empirical performance gains in Table 2 (Multi-target SBDD) and Table 1 are relatively modest, with standard deviations overlapping across several metrics.

Hyperparameter Sensitivity of (ca, cb): As shown in Section 5 and Appendix B.2, the optimal choice of (ca, cb) involves a delicate trade-off between effective sample size (ESS) and sample quality/diversity that appears task- and landscape-dependent (e.g., unimodal vs multimodal targets). A principled heuristic or adaptive selection rule for these parameters would strengthen the practical utility.

Small Sample Size and High Variance in Drug Design Benchmarks: In Section 5 and Appendix D.2/D.3, only 32 ligands are sampled per target pocket across 15–20 targets, leading to substantial variance in the reported metrics.

Lack of Wall-Clock / Runtime Profiling: Although the paper notes that per-step updates avoid looking back across full trajectories, a concrete wall-clock runtime and memory comparison against unguided diffusion, standard guidance, and FKC is not provided.

strengths: Unifying and elegant conceptual perspective: The paper successfully unifies several seemingly distinct existing approaches—including Itô density estimators, Feynman-Kac density estimators/correctors, and Twisted Diffusion Samplers—under the simple, foundational principle of path-space Radon–Nikodym derivatives between time-reversal processes.

Bypassing costly and restrictive operations: Unlike ODE-based continuous change-of-variables (which requires divergence computations) or prior FKC derivations for reward tilting (which require Hessian/Laplacian terms of the reward function), RNE and RNC operate in a plug-and-play fashion with Gaussian transition kernels and first-order quantities, naturally extending to non-differentiable rewards via Tweedie estimates.

Effective practical stabilization via analytical reference: The authors identify a key numerical instability in naive discrete Euler–Maruyama evaluation of path ratios under rapidly changing noise schedules (Eq. 32) and solve it systematically by introducing an analytical Gaussian reference process, backed by a non-asymptotic $O(\sqrt{\Delta t})$ convergence proof.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Experiments span toy multimodal targets, Boltzmann generation/annealing (ALDP and LJ-13), multi-target structure-based drug design (product composition), and controllable reward-tilting, showing competitive or superior performance over established baselines.
weaknesses: Heuristic selection of sampling/target drifts ($c_a, c_b$): While the flexibility to choose $a_t$ and $b_t$ independently of exact time-reversal is an advantage, the optimal balance between $c_a$ and $c_b$ remains task-dependent (as illustrated by the divergent behavior between ALDP and LJ-13 in Appendix B.2), with no automated heuristic provided to set them a priori.

Incremental empirical margins over FKC on some tasks: On the multi-target SBDD benchmark (Table 2), the quantitative improvements over FKC are somewhat modest (e.g., $0.649$ vs $0.608$ in 'Better than known', and comparable top-1 docking scores within error bars), although RNE achieves this with greater conceptual simplicity and implementation ease.

Inherent SMC limitations: As acknowledged in the limitations, SMC-based steering inevitably suffers from particle degeneracy/diversity reduction at small particle budgets ($M=32$ or $M=500$), which is evident in the reduced molecular fingerprint diversity.

strengths: Unifying Conceptual Framework: The paper provides an elegant, intuitive perspective unifying several existing continuous- and discrete-time techniques—such as the Itô density estimator, Feynman–Kac estimators, Twisted Diffusion Sampler (TDS), and Feynman–Kac Correctors (FKC)—under the fundamental concept of Radon–Nikodym derivatives between path measures.

Thorough Analysis of Discretization Instability: The authors clearly identify and mathematically analyze the variance misalignment problem that occurs when naively discretizing path measures under non-constant noise schedules (Section 4 and Appendix A.3). The proposed analytical Gaussian reference process effectively alleviates this issue and comes with a theoretical convergence guarantee of order O(sqrt(Delta t)).

Enhanced SMC Flexibility: By moving away from restrictive drift constraints imposed by PDE cancellations (as in FKC), the RNC formulation allows flexible tuning of proposal and target drifts (e.g., via hyperparameters c_a, c_b), which can be tuned to improve effective sample size and mitigate mode collapse in multimodal targets.

Interesting Scientific Applications: The experimental evaluation spans beyond toy synthetic distributions to physically meaningful domains, including molecular conformation annealing (Alanine Dipeptide, Lennard-Jones) and multi-target structure-based drug design (SBDD).
weaknesses: Incremental Conceptual Novelty: The core building blocks—Radon–Nikodym derivatives of path measures, time-reversal identities, reference processes (Vargas et al., 2023a/b), and SMC with diffusion proposals—are largely known in stochastic thermodynamics and recent diffusion literature. The method substantially overlaps with Skreta et al. (2024, 2025) and Wu et al. (2023), with many results being formal equivalences under specific drift choices.

Heuristic Drift Design and Hyperparameter Sensitivity: While RNC broadens the design space by decoupling sampling and target drifts, selecting the optimal drift coefficients (c_a, c_b) remains largely heuristic and problem-dependent (as demonstrated in Section 5 and Appendix B.2). There is no automated or principled criterion for setting them a priori without knowing target properties.

Evaluation Scope and Missing Baselines: The empirical validation lacks evaluation on standard high-dimensional vision or audio benchmarks commonly used in diffusion inference control. Additionally, for the reward-tilting experiment (Table 3), the method is only compared against an unguided baseline, omitting standard guidance baselines such as DPS, TDS, or classifier-based SMC steering.

Modest Empirical Gains with High Variance: On multi-target SBDD (Table 2), the improvements over FKC are relatively small and accompanied by high standard deviations across the 20 target pairs, making it difficult to assess statistical significance.

strengths: Unifying and elegant conceptual framework: The manuscript provides a principled, unifying perspective linking marginal densities, time-reversals, and transition kernels via the Radon-Nikodym derivative (RND = 1) between path measures. It successfully unifies and generalises several seemingly distinct methods, including Itô density estimators, Feynman-Kac steering/correctors, twisted diffusion samplers, and Fokker-Planck regularisers.

Methodological flexibility: By formulating inference-time control through path-space RND, the proposed RN Corrector (RNC) decouples the proposal and target processes, allowing broader algorithmic exploration (e.g., flexible tuning of drifts $a_t$ and $b_t$) without modifying the core SMC pipeline or requiring task-specific PDE derivations.

Principled solution to numerical instability: The identification of the variance misalignment issue in discretised forward/backward kernels and its resolution via an analytical Gaussian reference process is neat, practically effective, and supported by a non-asymptotic convergence rate analysis ($O(\sqrt{\Delta t})$).

Cheaper, divergence-free energy-based diffusion regularisation: The RNE regularisation enforces the marginal density relationship across time steps without computing or estimating the Jacobian trace / score divergence, offering a practical advantage over standard Fokker-Planck regularization.

Thorough theoretical and empirical validation on physically grounded tasks: The paper backs up its claims with detailed proofs across continuous SDEs and discrete CTMCs, along with diverse experiments on alanine dipeptide (ALDP), Lennard-Jones systems, multi-target structure-based drug design, and thermodynamic integration.
weaknesses: Limited evaluation on standard large-scale generative benchmarks: While the molecular and scientific benchmarks (ALDP, SBDD, thermodynamic integration) are well-suited for evaluating accurate density and energy properties, the paper lacks experiments on large-scale text-to-image or standard continuous benchmarks (e.g., CIFAR/ImageNet guidance or composition), which would broaden its appeal to the wider generative modeling community.

Hyperparameter sensitivity for drift heuristics: The superior performance of RNC over FKC relies on introducing and choosing drift split parameters $(c_a, c_b)$. As observed in the experiments on ALDP vs. LJ-13, the optimal choice depends on target modality/peakedness, and there is currently no closed-form or automated heuristic for choosing these coefficients a priori.

Scope of exact SMC weight cancellation: As honestly noted in Section 2.1.3 and Appendix C.5, exact cancellation under imperfect diffusion models holds only for reward-tilting; for annealing and model composition, model approximation and discretisation errors cannot be fully canceled, leaving residual bias in practical deployments.

strengths: Conceptual Elegance and Unification: The paper provides a clean, unified perspective connecting marginal density estimation, Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) inference-time steering, and energy-based diffusion training through the lens of Radon-Nikodym derivatives between time-reversal path measures. It successfully unifies and generalizes several existing methods (e.g., Feynman-Kac Correctors, Twisted Diffusion Sampler, Itô Density Estimators, and Fokker-Planck regularizers).

Practical and Divergence-Free Formulation: Unlike standard continuous-time formulations that require computing or estimating costly trace/divergence terms (or Hessian-vector products / Laplacians), RNE/RNC can be computed directly using discretized transition kernels (Gaussian kernels), dramatically simplifying implementation while reducing computational overhead.

Principled Stabilization via Analytical Reference: The authors identify a key numerical pathology—namely, kernel variance misalignment during discretization when noise scales vary—and propose an elegant resolution using an analytical Gaussian reference process. The theoretical convergence rate bound of O(sqrt(Delta t)) for the reference-based estimator is well-derived and solid.

Comprehensive and Impactful Applications: The methodology is thoroughly validated across challenging real-world tasks, including molecular conformation annealing (Alanine Dipeptide, Lennard-Jones), multi-target structure-based drug design, energy-based diffusion regularisation, and thermodynamic integration for solvation free energy estimation.
weaknesses: Heuristic Hyperparameter Selection for (ca, cb): The flexibility introduced by uncoupling proposal and target drifts is a key conceptual advantage over FKC, but the performance is sensitive to the choice of (ca, cb) (as shown in Figure 2 and Figure 11). The paper provides useful intuition regarding ESS vs. mode coverage, but lacks an automated or adaptive heuristic for selecting optimal coefficients without access to ground truth.

Lack of Empirical Validation for CTMC: While Section 2.3 and Appendix D formally extend RNE to Continuous-Time Markov Chains (CTMC), this extension remains entirely theoretical. Demonstrating the discrete formulation on a benchmark (e.g., discrete sequence generation or text) would strengthen the claim of generality across modalities.

Marginal Gains on Multi-Target SBDD: In the multi-target SBDD ligand design benchmark (Table 3), while RNC outperforms the heuristic score sum baseline and provides slightly better 'Better than known' docking percentages, many metrics overlap with FKC within reported standard errors.

Notation and Density in Main Text: The notation involves multiple pairs of drifts and reverse drifts (mu, nu, a, b, f, v, sigma, epsilon) alongside both forward and backward path measures. While the appendix does an admirable job explaining every step, the main text can occasionally be difficult to follow on a first read.

strengths: Unifying Conceptual Framework: The paper provides an elegant and coherent perspective connecting path-space Radon–Nikodym derivatives of time-reversal SDEs to marginal density ratios. This successfully links and unifies several recently proposed, seemingly disparate methods in diffusion density estimation (Itô density estimator, Feynman–Kac density relation), inference-time control (Twisted Diffusion Sampler, Feynman–Kac correctors), and energy-based training (Fokker–Planck regularisation).

Divergence-Free Computation: By formulating the path ratios directly through transition kernels (or Gaussian discrete-time transition densities), the framework bypasses the expensive divergence/trace estimation required by probability flow ODEs or score Jacobian computations in continuous-time Fokker–Planck/Feynman–Kac equations.

Identification and Resolution of Discretization Instability: The paper identifies a crucial practical issue—the variance mismatch between forward and backward transition kernels under time-varying diffusion schedules—and provides an analytical Gaussian reference process to stabilize estimation, backed by theoretical non-asymptotic convergence bounds (Proposition G.1).

Diverse Application Suite: The method is validated across a wide array of meaningful applications, including inference-time annealing (alanine dipeptide and LJ-13), multi-target structure-based drug design (SBDD), energy-based model training on high-dimensional GMMs and molecular force fields, and thermodynamic integration for solvation free energies.
weaknesses: Nuanced Exactness Guarantees: While exact SMC weights can be computed for imperfect models in the reward-tilting setting (Proposition 2.2, recovering TDS/FKS), the authors correctly note in Appendix C.5 that this cancellation does not hold for annealing or model composition. In those settings, the validity strictly hinges on the assumption of a near-perfect diffusion model, which introduces bias in practical, imperfectly learned regimes.

Heuristic Process Parameterization: While the framework allows broader design flexibility for proposal and target drifts (parameterized by coefficients $c_a, c_b$) compared to rigid FKC formulations, finding optimal drift parameters appears non-trivial and task-dependent, exhibiting distinct trade-offs between effective sample size (ESS) and sample fidelity depending on target unimodality/multimodality.

Scope of Empirical Benchmarks: Although the experiments across molecular systems and GMMs are technically appropriate and standard in the AI-for-science domain, the paper lacks large-scale generative benchmarks (e.g., standard image synthesis or text generation with discrete CTMC diffusion), leaving the scalability to large foundational models less explored.

Incremental Foundational Novelty: The core mathematical equivalence (path measure ratios between forward and reverse processes equating to marginal density ratios) is deeply rooted in established nonequilibrium physics (Jarzynski/Crooks relations) and stochastic control; thus, the contribution lies primarily in algorithmic synthesis, unification, and application rather than fundamentally novel theoretical mechanisms.
